subject: Why does efa in lavaan produces different results than psych::fa?

messages.author: dc9fab12f3703014
messages.subject: Why does efa in lavaan produces different results than psych::fa?
parts:
Hi all,

I tried to replicate the results from psych::fa() with lavaan::efa(). Same data, same rotation, but got different chi^2. Is there a plausible reason for this behavior that I have overlooked? And might there be a way to match results between packages?

Greetings
Matze

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Why does efa in lavaan produces different results than psych::fa?
parts:
On 11/29/22 20:53, 'Matthias Kloft' via lavaan wrote:
> I tried to replicate the results from psych::fa() with lavaan::efa().
> Same data, same rotation, but got different chi^2. Is there a plausible
> reason for this behavior that I have overlooked? And might there be a
> way to match results between packages?

[This reminds me of similar questions regarding differences between
Mplus and lavaan.]

I have not studied the psych package in depth, so I don't know how
exactly the fa() function works. But I do believe that fa() is using the
algorithms from the EFA literature for factor extraction, while lavaan
is using algorithms from the CFA literature. In theory (for complete
continuous unclustered data) this should lead to identical results, but
I would not be surprised to see some small discrepancies. I would also
not be too concerned about this, especially if are talking about numbers
after the decimal point.

To get more similar results, there are a few things you could try: On
the psych::fa() side, you should set fm = "ml", as this is (currently)
the default in lavaan. On the lavaan side, you could set likelihood =
"Wishart", as this will use 'N=1' (instead of N) in several places. But
it is still unlikely that the Chi-square values will match exactly.

For what it is worth, lavaan's Chi-square values do match exactly the
values reported by Mplus when using type = EFA.

If you do find examples where the differences seem rather large, please
send them to me (per email). Then I will investigate and try to
understand where the discrepancies are coming from.

Yves.

messages.author: dc9fab12f3703014
messages.subject: Re: Why does efa in lavaan produces different results than psych::fa?
parts:
Hello Yves,

thanks for the detailed explanation!
The "ml" method in fa() and the Wishart likelihood did mitigate the difference a little bit. The difference was not large enough to change the conclusions anyways. Also, my sample was very small to begin with.
Thanks for implementing the efa! I am very happy that I can now do all the modeling in one framework.

Greetings
Matze
